args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC.
PROJECT LATTICE
ESCALATION MEMORANDUM — ARTICLE VIII (INDEMNIFICATION) — HALBERD SECOND-TURN MARKUP

To: The Special Committee of the Board of Directors, Trellis BioWorks, Inc.
From: Trellis Deal Team (Project Lattice)
Date: 31 July 2026
Re: Escalation of Halberd Holdings second-turn markup of SPA Article VIII (Indemnification); requests exceed deal team delegated authority and require Special Committee approval

------------------------------------------------------------------
I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
------------------------------------------------------------------
Halberd Holdings LP's outside counsel, Wexler Bright LLP, transmitted a second-turn markup of Article VIII (Indemnification) to the Share Purchase Agreement on 30 July 2026, marked against our sell-side execution draft v4. This memorandum (1) compares each markup change against the current v4 position and the deal team's approved fallback (Transaction Committee-approved positions of 24 July 2026); (2) quantifies cap and basket deltas in dollars against the Purchase Price; (3) identifies which Halberd asks exceed the deal team's delegated authority and therefore require Special Committee approval; (4) addresses the proposed special indemnity by reference to the specific Schedule 3.14 disclosed items it would cover; and (5) sets out our recommendation and approval request.

For ease of reference: the Purchase Price is $120,000,000. Execution draft v4 carries an indemnity cap of 10% of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000) and a true deductible of $400,000. The Transaction Committee approved the following fallbacks on 24 July 2026: survival of general representations up to twenty-four (24) months (IP-1); an indemnity cap up to fifteen percent (15%) of the Purchase Price, i.e., $18,000,000 (IP-2); a true deductible reducible to a floor of $300,000 but in no event convertible to a tipping basket (IP-3); and a special indemnity for disclosed matters only if scope-limited to Schedule 3.14 Items 1 and 2, capped at $2,500,000, with twenty-four (24) month survival, and expressly excluding resolved matters such as Item 3 (IP-4).

------------------------------------------------------------------
II. LINE-BY-LINE COMPARISON OF THE HALBERD MARKUP
------------------------------------------------------------------

Change 1 — Section 8.1 (Survival of general representations): 18 months → 36 months.
• v4 position: general representations survive eighteen (18) months.
• Halberd ask: thirty-six (36) months.
• Deal team approved fallback: maximum twenty-four (24) months (IP-1).
• Assessment: The 36-month ask exceeds the approved 24-month fallback by twelve (12) months and is expressly flagged "out of policy" under IP-1. This change materially extends contingent liability exposure beyond the deal team's delegated authority.
• DELEGATED AUTHORITY: EXCEEDED — requires Special Committee approval.

Change 2 — Section 8.3(a) (Basket/Deductible): true deductible $400,000 → tipping basket $250,000.
• v4 position: a true deductible of $400,000 — the Sellers have no liability under Section 8.2(a) until aggregate Losses exceed $400,000, and only for the excess.
• Halberd ask: conversion to a "tipping basket" of $250,000 — once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000, the Sellers are liable from the first dollar.
• Deal team approved fallback: the basket must remain a true deductible; conversion to a tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold. The deductible may be reduced from $400,000 but not below a floor of $300,000 (IP-3).
• Assessment: The Halberd ask both (a) reduces the threshold below the $300,000 floor (to $250,000) and, more fundamentally, (b) converts the structure from a true deductible to a tipping/first-dollar basket, which is categorically out of policy. Both elements exceed delegated authority.
• DELEGATED AUTHORITY: EXCEEDED — requires Special Committee approval.

Change 3 — Section 8.3(b) (Cap): 10% → 25% of Purchase Price.
• v4 position: aggregate cap of ten percent (10%) of Purchase Price = $12,000,000.
• Halberd ask: twenty-five percent (25%) of Purchase Price = $30,000,000.
• Deal team approved fallback: maximum fifteen percent (15%) of Purchase Price = $18,000,000 (IP-2).
• Assessment: The ask exceeds the approved cap on every basis.
• Cap delta in dollars: v4 cap is $12,000,000; approved fallback cap is $18,000,000; Halberd ask is $30,000,000.
  • Delta vs. v4: $30,000,000 − $12,000,000 = +$18,000,000.
  • Delta vs. approved fallback: $30,000,000 − $18,000,000 = +$12,000,000.
  • The ask would add $18,000,000 of on-the-books indemnity exposure over the current v4 cap, and $12,000,000 over the maximum the deal team is authorized to concede.
• The 25% ask exceeds the 15% fallback and is flagged "out of policy" under IP-2.
• DELEGATED AUTHORITY: EXCEEDED — requires Special Committee approval.

Change 4 — NEW Section 8.2(d) (Special Indemnity for Schedule 3.14 matters), uncapped and outside the Deductible/Cap.
• v4 position: execution draft v4 contains no special indemnities.
• Halberd ask: the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, with that indemnity NOT subject to the Deductible or the cap in Section 8.3, and surviving until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation.
• Deal team approved fallback (IP-4): a special indemnity is acceptable ONLY if all of the following hold: (i) scope limited to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2 (the pending matters); (ii) aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of twenty-four (24) months from Closing; and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.
• Assessment against Schedule 3.14:
  • The proposed special indemnity is not capped (violates IP-4(ii), which requires an aggregate $2,500,000 cap).
  • It is not subject to the Deductible or the Cap (consistent with the out-of-policy refusal to cap).
  • Its survival extends to the expiration of applicable statutes of limitation, far beyond the approved twenty-four (24) months (violates IP-4(iii)).
  • Critically, its scope reads to "the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14" across the schedule, without confining coverage to the pending Item 1 and Item 2 or excluding resolved matters. Read literally it would sweep in Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — the resolved OSHA citation (Citation No. 1829445), which was resolved by informal settlement, its $46,500 penalty paid in full on 17 March 2026, and its abatement certified 2 March 2026. IP-4(iv) expressly requires exclusion of resolved matters including Item 3. This violates IP-4(i) and IP-4(iv).
  • The schedule items the special indemnity would actually cover if confined to the pending matters (per the approved position) are:
      - Item 1: the pending TTAB trademark opposition (Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc.) opposing registration of the TRELLIGEN mark (U.S. App. Serial No. 98/415,882). No damages are claimed; exposure is potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line.
      - Item 2: the pending pre-litigation customer dispute with Bexley Clinical Partners LLC, which claims $1,850,000 in damages for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement. The Company denied liability on 24 April 2026; the insurer was noticed 28 April 2026 with coverage position reserved.
  • As drafted, however, the Halberd special indemnity is unlimited in amount, uncapped, and facially extends beyond the two pending items to resolved matters, all of which is out of policy.
• The requested special indemnity in the form proposed exceeds delegated authority in every material respect.
• DELEGATED AUTHORITY: EXCEEDED — requires Special Committee approval.

Change 5 — Section 8.5 (Order of Recovery): conforming change permitting special-indemnity recovery directly from the Sellers without first exhausting the Escrow Amount.
• v4 position: Buyer recovers first from the Escrow Amount, then severally from the Sellers pro rata.
• Halberd ask: special-indemnity claims recoverable directly from the Sellers without exhausting the Escrow Amount.
• Assessment: This conforming change is derivative of the proposed special indemnity (Change 4). It is acceptable in principle as a conforming adjustment, but only if the special indemnity itself is conformed to the deal team's approved parameters. As proposed, it further amplifies exposure by directing recovery away from the escrow before Sellers' collateral is tapped.
• DELEGATED AUTHORITY: contingent on Change 4; as attached to the current out-of-policy special indemnity, EXCEEDED — requires Special Committee approval.

------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DOLLAR QUANTIFICATION OF CAP AND BASKET DELTAS (vs. $120,000,000 Purchase Price)
------------------------------------------------------------------
• Cap (Section 8.3(b)):
  • v4: 10% = $12,000,000
  • Approved fallback: 15% = $18,000,000
  • Halberd ask: 25% = $30,000,000
  • Delta vs. v4: +$18,000,000
  • Delta vs. approved fallback: +$12,000,000
  • Amount exceeding the deal team's delegated authority: $12,000,000.
• Basket/Deductible (Section 8.3(a)):
  • v4: true deductible $400,000 (excess-only recovery)
  • Approved fallback floor: $300,000 (true deductible)
  • Halberd ask: tipping basket $250,000 (first-dollar recovery once exceeded)
  • Threshold delta vs. v4: −$150,000 (from $400,000 to $250,000), which also breaches the $300,000 floor by $50,000.
  • Structural delta: conversion from excess-only true deductible to first-dollar tipping basket is a qualitative escalation that, once triggered, exposes the Sellers to Losses from the first dollar rather than only the excess — materially increasing recoverable exposure beyond the dollar-shift alone. This structure is categorically out of policy.
• Special indemnity: uncapped, so no finite cap delta can be stated; it removes the Deductible and Cap entirely for Schedule 3.14 matters and eliminates any dollar ceiling, exposing the Sellers to the full (and in the case of Item 2, $1,850,000-claimed) amounts without the protection of the indemnity limits.

------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. ASKS EXCEEDING THE DEAL TEAM'S DELEGATED AUTHORITY
------------------------------------------------------------------
Every substantive Halberd markup change in this transmittal exceeds the deal team's delegated authority as memorialized in the 24 July 2026 Transaction Committee-approved positions:
  1. Survival of 36 months (Change 1) — exceeds approved 24-month fallback (IP-1).
  2. Tipping basket of $250,000 (Change 2) — conversion to tipping structure is out of policy, and threshold breaches the $300,000 floor (IP-3).
  3. Cap of 25% / $30,000,000 (Change 3) — exceeds approved 15% / $18,000,000 fallback by $12,000,000 (IP-2).
  4. Uncapped special indemnity sweeping Schedule 3.14 broadly, outside the Deductible/Cap, surviving to SOL expiration (Change 4) — violates all four IP-4 conditions (scope limited to Items 1–2, $2,500,000 cap, 24-month survival, exclusion of resolved Item 3).
  5. Reordering recovery to bypass the escrow (Change 5) — contingent on the out-of-policy special indemnity.

Accordingly, the deal team is not authorized to accept any of these concessions on its own; each requires Special Committee approval, and the deal team recommends the Committee reject the markup largely as proposed and instead counter within the approved fallback envelope.

------------------------------------------------------------------
V. RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVAL REQUEST
------------------------------------------------------------------
Recommendation. We recommend the Special Committee reject the Halberd second-turn indemnity package in its current form and direct the deal team to respond with a counter that holds to the approved fallback envelope, specifically:
  • Survival: counter at a maximum of twenty-four (24) months (IP-1), declining 36 months.
  • Basket: hold a true deductible (declining the tipping basket outright), and, if concessions are needed, reduce the deductible toward the $300,000 floor but not below it (IP-3).
  • Cap: counter at a maximum of fifteen percent (15%) / $18,000,000 (IP-2), declining 25% / $30,000,000.
  • Special indemnity: decline the uncapped, no-deductible/no-cap special indemnity as proposed. If a special indemnity is to be conceded, offer one strictly confined to Schedule 3.14 Items 1 and 2 (the pending trademark opposition and the Bexley customer dispute), capped at $2,500,000, with twenty-four (24) month survival, and expressly excluding resolved Item 3 (the OSHA citation) (IP-4). The conforming Order of Recovery change should then be tied to that conformed scope.
  • Logistics: all responsive work product will be filed in the Trellis matter workspace under Trellis naming conventions only and not under counterparty-proposed filenames, data-room mirroring requests, or transmittal logistics (IP-5), consistent with our internal filing rules.

Approval request. We respectfully request the Special Committee approve the recommended counter-position set forth above, and specifically (1) authorize rejection of the proposed 36-month survival, $250,000 tipping basket, 25%/$30,000,000 cap, and the uncapped broad special indemnity; and (2) authorize the deal team to counter within the fallback envelope, including a potential special indemnity limited to Schedule 3.14 Items 1 and 2 at a $2,500,000 cap with 24-month survival and express exclusion of resolved Item 3. Absent such approval, the deal team will not offer or accept any concession beyond the Fall-2026 approved fallbacks.

Respectfully submitted,
Trellis Deal Team — Project Lattice
